This study looks at how Wordtune, as an AI tool, can facilitate the writing process of intermediate-level EFL students at the Department of Applied Foreign Languages, Tatung University in Taiwan. The selection of Wordtune in this research targets a major challenge for Taiwanese learners that I have been observing for years in my EFL writing classes, namely, their tendency to write generalizations without specific details due to their Chinese ways of thinking, regardless of what genres they are writing. With an AI tool such as Wordtune, students are more likely to get instant feedback on the language scaffolding in their writing process in order to communicate more effectively, as long as AI has been used wisely and ethically. The study analyses how the facilitation of Wordtune helps the paragraph structure and idea development of 25 students across five writing genres: narration, description, classification, cause and effect, and problem-solution. A comparative analysis was conducted between self-revised and AI-enhanced versions of students’ writing. Results indicate that the implementation of Wordtune as an AI tool, together with proper instruction, raised metacognitive awareness of their writing problems. The findings highlight the potential of AI to support intermediate EFL learners in overcoming L1 interference and improving the coherence and specificity of their writing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20319/ictel.2025.443444\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 8, 13]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-3373-9650-7.ch010\", \"title\": [\"Simulation-Based Education for Neurosurgical Training Using AI\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Simulation-based education has developed into a revolutionar…

The study analyses how the facilitation of Wordtune helps the paragraph structure and idea development of 25 students across five writing genres: narration, description, classification, cause and effect, and problem-solution. The findings highlight the potential of AI to support intermediate EFL learners in overcoming L1 interference and improving the coherence and specificity of their writing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20319/ictel.2025.443444\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 8, 13]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-3373-9650-7.ch010\", \"title\": [\"Simulation-Based Education for Neurosurgical Training Using AI\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Simulation-based education has developed into a revolutionary training method for neurosurgical education, which provides solutions to the shortcomings of traditional apprenticeship systems that depend on actual patient contact and their method of evaluating students. The research investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) works together with virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR) advanced simulation systems to improve neurosurgery skill acquisition and decision-making and competency-based learning. AI systems provide assessment of performance in real time along with customized feedback and learning paths that adjust to individual needs, which enables students to master advanced techniques within a secure training space. The research uses a mixed-methods approach to assess how well an AI-based simulation platform performs by using quantitative performance data and qualitative feedback from trainees and experts.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-3373-9650-7.ch010\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 24]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1186/isrctn15993331\", \"title\": [\"AI-assisted clinical decision-making training for pharmacology students\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1186/isrctn15993331\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 6, 26]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1257/rct.19216\", \"title\": [\"AI Integration in Hiring:\\nA Randomized Experiment\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.19216\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 8, 18]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "6e13dd72006771a5a7865ad40d4045dba88f13aaf5572d076cd883ff9d21c923", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "emergent_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.20319/ictel.2025.443444", "doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9650-7.ch010", "doi:10.1186/isrctn15993331", "doi:10.1257/rct.19216"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.20319/ictel.2025.443444", "https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-3373-9650-7.ch010", "https://doi.org/10.1186/isrctn15993331", "https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.19216"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
